prompt.context: Oil Co is a holding company that manages a portfolio of companies related to oil exploration. The portfolio can be segmented as: (1) an oil rig managed and operated by Oil Co., and (2) a group of companies (including Oil Co.) that have a proportional stake in an oil rig, with each company sharing costs and profits. Oil Co. wants to increase its profitability and has come to McKinsey for ideas.
prompt.question: What are the key areas you would look at to help Oil Co. increase its profitability?

clarifying_info.q: Is Oil Co. willing to divest any of its holdings?
clarifying_info.a: No, the company is not willing to divest any holdings.

clarifying_info.q: Can the contracts with partner companies be renegotiated?
clarifying_info.a: No, existing contracts under segment 2 are iron clad and cannot be modified.

clarifying_info.q: Is the goal purely profitability, or also revenue growth?
clarifying_info.a: Profitability is Oil Co.'s only concern.

clarifying_info.q: Are the oil rigs onshore or offshore?
clarifying_info.a: All oil rigs are operated offshore.

clarifying_info.q: Can Oil Co. explore new areas to set up additional rigs?
clarifying_info.a: No, the company does not know of any new areas to explore.
Oil Co. is a British company.

clarifying_info.q: What is the FX rate between USD and GBP?
How many days per year does the rig operate?

exhibits.title: Cost Data for Oil Rig Operations
exhibits.shows: A summary of current transportation costs and operating costs for the oil rig, along with proposed reduction scenarios
exhibits.data: Transportation costs: currently 50MM GBP per year, can be reduced to $100,000 per day; Operating costs: currently $40MM, can be reduced by 30%

framework: Recognize this is a cost savings case — revenue levers are unavailable (no new rigs, no contract changes, no divestiture)
Segment costs into major categories: (1) transportation costs to/from the rig, (2) operating expenses on the rig
Evaluate feasibility and magnitude of reductions in each cost category
Quantify total savings in absolute dollars and as a percentage of current total costs
Prioritize initiatives and present a clear recommendation

questions.prompt: How would you cut costs on an oil rig, given the constraints?
questions.guidance: Candidate should eliminate unavailable options (closing rigs, changing schedules, exploring new areas, widening pipes, changing partner contracts) and focus only on two viable levers: (1) reducing operating expenses, and (2) reducing transportation costs to/from the rig. Interviewer should push back on any ideas outside these two buckets.

questions.prompt: Transportation costs are currently 50MM GBP per year and can be reduced to $100,000 per day. What are the savings in USD?
questions.guidance: Candidate must convert GBP to USD, compute new annual cost at the reduced daily rate, and find the difference.

math.setup: Current cost in USD = 50MM GBP × $1.5/GBP. New annual cost = $100,000/day × 365 days. Savings = current USD cost − new annual cost.

questions.prompt: Operating costs are currently $40MM and can be reduced by 30%. What are the savings?
questions.guidance: Straightforward percentage calculation on the operating cost base.

questions.prompt: What are the total savings, and what percentage of current total costs does that represent?
questions.guidance: Candidate should sum both savings figures and divide by total current costs (converting all figures to USD first).

math.setup: Total current costs = transportation ($75MM) + operating ($40MM) = $115MM. Total savings = $38.5MM + $12MM.
math.answer: Total savings of $50.5MM, representing approximately 44% of current total costs

brainstorming.prompt: What specific ideas could reduce operating expenses on an offshore oil rig?

categories.name: Labor
ideas: Renegotiate labor contracts or shift to lower-cost labor markets
Optimize crew rotation schedules to reduce idle time

categories.name: Energy & Fuel
ideas: Improve fuel efficiency of rig machinery
Switch to lower-cost energy sources where feasible
Implement energy monitoring to reduce waste

categories.name: Maintenance
ideas: Shift from reactive to preventive maintenance to reduce emergency repair costs
Consolidate vendor contracts for maintenance services
Use condition-based monitoring to extend equipment life

categories.name: Procurement & Supplies
ideas: Consolidate purchasing to gain volume discounts
Switch to lower-cost but equivalent suppliers
Reduce inventory holding costs through just-in-time delivery

categories.name: Transportation & Logistics
ideas: Consolidate supply runs to reduce trip frequency
Use helicopters only for urgent personnel transfers

recommendation: Oil Co. should pursue both available cost levers: reduce transportation costs from $75MM to $36.5MM per year ($38.5MM savings) and reduce operating costs by 30% ($12MM savings)
Total projected annual savings of $50.5MM represent a 44% reduction in current total costs of $115MM
risks: Operational risk if cost reductions compromise safety or maintenance standards on offshore rigs
Execution risk in achieving the full 30% operating cost reduction — requires detailed implementation planning
Currency risk: savings are partially denominated in USD while Oil Co. is a British company
next_steps: Conduct detailed operational audit to identify specific line items driving the 30% operating cost reduction
Develop an RFP or renegotiation process for transportation contracts to achieve the $100K/day target
Establish a monitoring framework to track realized savings versus targets on a quarterly basis
